You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.

You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule: TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return

Preferred position:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.


Fallback position:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

Drafter's locked target level: preferred

Original clause:
10. EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION
10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.
10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.

Rendered redlined clause:
10. EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION
10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.
10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) provide transition assistance for up to 6 months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within 30 days of expiry or termination, return all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format; and (c) after such return, delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Juniper Ridge Health, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Cobalt Cloud Services LLC, a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Juniper Ridge Health, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Cobalt Cloud Services LLC, a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Customer Data: 1.3 “Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.
Deliverable: 1.4 “Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.
Fees: 1.5 “Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.
Services: 1.7 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-lol-cap-89120a73","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","rationale":"Section 21.1 sets a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, which matches our preferred position. The floor is not illusory: \"Fees\" (Section 1.5) covers recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, and Section 2.1 commits USD 2,000,000 of Services per year, so 12 months' Fees will normally exceed the USD 1,000,000 alternative. Section 21.2 contains a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and helpfully confirms that data restoration, replacement services, required notices and reasonable incident response are direct damages. Section 21.3 defines \"Excluded Claims\" to cover confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other Party's IP; because both 21.1 and 21.2 open with \"Except for Excluded Claims\", those claims sit outside the cap and the damages exclusion, so indemnities are not capped. Section 21.3 also confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not damages and is not limited by the Section, and Section 21.4 keeps each cap independent and effective on failure of an exclusive remedy. Nothing is one-sided against Customer, so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-329c36c9","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","rationale":"Section 24 meets the preferred position in full: 24.1 lets us assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor consent (notice only); 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our consent (reasonableness-qualified) and never to a direct competitor; and 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on our change of control. Section 24.3's mutual consent requirement is scoped to \"other assignments,\" so it is a residual catch-all and does not swallow the 24.1 carve-out; the consent standard there is also fully qualified (\"withheld, conditioned, or delayed\"). Section 13.3 reinforces the position by allowing licence rights to travel with a Section 24-permitted assignment. Section 9.2's insolvency termination right is mutual and expressly excludes a lawful reorganization that does not impair performance, so it creates no back-door change-of-control exit. No redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-416a3ca9","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 27.3 If a force-majeure event materially prevents an affected Service for more than fifteen consecutive days, Customer may procure substitute services and suspend affected Fees. After thirty consecutive days, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without penalty and receive a refund of prepaid Fees for the unavailable period.","rationale":"The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum fee payable by Customer. Full-text searches for \"liquidated damages\", \"penalty\", \"early termination\", and \"termination fee\" return nothing adverse: the only \"penalty\" reference (§ 27.3) confirms Customer may terminate without penalty, § 7.3 bars interest on amounts found not due, and the § 22.2 audit shortfall/cost recovery is compensatory rather than a stipulated penalty. This meets the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages). The § 2.1 take-or-pay commitment is the nearest economic exposure, but it is a volume commitment addressed under the minimum-commitment rule and is not flagged again here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-f190ec3e","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.","rationale":"§ 22 meets the preferred position on every material term: audits are limited to once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, off-site where practicable, and by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (§ 22.1). § 22.2 places audit costs on Vendor unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent, and expressly bars Vendor and its auditor from accessing Customer systems directly, unrelated Customer Data, privileged material or third-party confidential information — so there is no direct or remote system access. § 22.3 additionally protects us by making findings Customer Confidential Information and limiting their use. No other inspection or verification right binding us appears elsewhere in the document. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-efa4e44f","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.","rationale":"The renewal mechanics meet the preferred position in full. § 8.2 provides automatic renewals of twelve months only (no multi-year auto-renewal), a Customer opt-out on just thirty days' written notice (well inside the ≤30-day preferred window), and a Vendor reminder sixty days before renewal — plus an extra protection for us, since a missed reminder extends our opt-out deadline to thirty days after the reminder arrives. § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI over the preceding twelve months and three percent, matching the preferred cap, with ninety days' notice of any increase and no increase on prepaid periods. The obligations here bind Vendor and the notice burden on us is minimal, so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-d9bcb5c0","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.","rationale":"Section 10 addresses only loss of access, Deliverable delivery and refunds. Nothing obliges Vendor to provide transition assistance (10.1 merely assumes \"any agreed transition period\" with no entitlement or pricing) or to return or export Customer Data in a usable format, and no deletion certification exists. Section 16.5 covers only Confidential Information return and defers Customer Data to Sections 11 and 15 — Section 11 does not exist in the document and Section 15 contains only processing-purpose and privacy-compliance duties. The rule's fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day data export) is therefore not met anywhere, so we insert a new 10.3 at the preferred position: up to six months' assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, machine-readable data return within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter (carve-outs for routine backups and legal retention mirroring 16.5).","proposal":"Insert new Section 10.3 requiring up to 6 months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion after return.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-warranty-0fcbd897","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 19.1 Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.","rationale":"Section 19 delivers the preferred position in full: 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty plus material conformity to documentation and specifications; 19.2 runs the Deliverable conformity warranty for ninety days from the later of delivery or acceptance and holds hosted Services to conformity for the entire subscription term (better than the 12-month software benchmark); 19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law, no malicious code and open-source/functionality protections. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel
**Re:** Playbook review — Master Services Agreement (Vendor form)
**Status:** For negotiation

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The liability, insurance, warranty, audit, assignment and renewal architecture is strong and needs no redlining — several provisions (mutual liability cap with uncapped Excluded Claims, cyber cover of USD 5,000,000, CPI-capped renewal uplift, missed-reminder extension) meet or exceed our preferred positions.

The difficulties are concentrated in two areas. First, there is a genuine drafting gap: **there is no indemnification clause at all**. The body runs from § 19.5 directly to § 21, with no Section 20, even though §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all cross-refer to indemnity obligations that do not exist. As drafted we would fund our own defence of third-party IP claims. We have inserted a new Section 20 at the preferred position, numbering the remedies subsection 20.5 so the existing § 9.3 cross-reference resolves.

Second, a cluster of clauses imposes one-sided restraints on us that are internally inconsistent with the Agreement's own § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made **no** exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment. Those clauses are §§ 2.1 (three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay without reduction or termination rights), 7.2 (disclose-and-match), 12.4 (24-month non-compete) and 12.4 (24-month no-hire). Each sits in walk-away territory on our playbook. We also have no termination for convenience against a three-year locked term, no transition-assistance or data-return obligation, Vendor ownership of every Deliverable under a revocable term-limited licence, and a Singapore governing law clause in § 28.1 that contradicts the New York jurisdiction clause in § 28.2.

We note one procedural point: the governing law finding did not clear our verification step and should be re-confirmed against the execution copy before it is put to Vendor.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2–21.4) |
| 2 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3, 9.2) |
| 3 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 27.3 (with §§ 7.3, 22.2) |
| 4 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with §§ 22.2–22.3) |
| 5 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 (with § 8.3) |
| 6 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 10.2 (gap; new § 10.3 proposed) |
| 7 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.2–19.5) |
| 8 | Low | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 |
| 9 | Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** *(verification failed — re-confirm)* | § 28.1 (conflicts with § 28.2) |
| 10 | Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | No Section 20 (gap between §§ 19.5 and 21) |
| 11 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) |
| 12 | Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 14.2 |
| 13 | Low | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 14.2 (§§ 13.1–13.3 compliant) |
| 14 | Low | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 |
| 15 | Low | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | **Deviation** | § 2.1 |
| 16 | Low | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 |
| 17 | Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 |
| 18 | Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 9.3 (gap; new § 9.4 proposed) |

### 2.1 Notes on the deviations and gaps

**§ 2.1 — Minimum commitment (MINCOMMIT).** A three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay expressly "without reduction or termination rights" is walk-away territory and falls short of our fallback (12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up rather than penalty). It also conflicts with § 12.3 and with the Order Form fee structure in § 7.1. We have replaced it with pay-for-what-is-ordered-or-used, and offered the fallback in comment.

**§ 7.2 — Disclose-and-match (EXCLUSIVITY and MFN).** This single provision breaches two rules independently: as a sourcing restraint it is a de facto right of first refusal with no category limit, no 12-month sunset and no performance-failure exit; as an MFN it runs the wrong way, obliging us to extend Vendor any better third-party terms with no comparability carve-outs. Both fail the respective fallbacks and both contradict § 12.3. Our redline deletes the obligation and confirms Vendor's non-exclusive status.

**§ 12.4 — Non-compete (NONCOMPETE).** A 24-month post-term restraint on developing, marketing, selling or acquiring "any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory," with no internal-development or acquisition carve-out. Deletion is the minimal fix and restores consistency with § 12.3.

**§ 12.4 — No-hire (NOSOLICIT).** This is a no-hire rather than a non-solicit, covering all Vendor employees for the term plus 24 months "regardless of how the employee applies." We have narrowed it to our fallback — mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire. Outright deletion remains acceptable to us.

**No Section 20 — Indemnification (INDEMN).** No indemnity exists anywhere; the contiguous numbering confirms a drafting gap rather than an extraction error. We have inserted a Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorised access to Customer Data, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, extended to Customer Affiliates, with customary IP exclusions, a notice/control/cooperation procedure with a no-adverse-settlement carve-out, procure-modify-replace-refund remedies at § 20.5, and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and our breach of law. No super-cap was added because § 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims outside the cap — better than our fallback.

**§ 14.2 — Deliverable ownership and licence (IP and LICENSE).** Vendor owns every Deliverable created specifically for us, and our licence is revocable, non-transferable and limited to the Order Form term. This fails both the preferred position (Customer ownership with assignment) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense). The § 13.2 perpetual licence does not cure it — that covers Vendor Technology and embedded paid-up software, not the Deliverable. Our redline flips assignment to us while preserving Vendor Technology under § 14.3, and conforms the licence terms to §§ 13.1–13.3 (Affiliates and contractors, revocation only for uncured material breach).

**New § 9.4 — Termination for convenience (T4C).** Section 9 offers cause-based exits only, against a three-year term and a take-or-pay commitment with no termination right. We have added a Customer-only right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, expressly overriding the § 2.1 no-termination language for the terminated Services. Vendor has no convenience right, which is acceptable to us.

**New § 10.3 — Transition and data return (TRANSITION).** Section 10 covers only loss of access, Deliverable delivery and refunds; § 16.5 defers Customer Data to Sections 11 and 15, but Section 11 does not exist and Section 15 covers only processing purpose and privacy compliance. We have inserted up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable data return within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter, with backup and legal-retention carve-outs mirroring § 16.5.

**§ 28.1 — Governing law (GOVLAW).** Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction is outside our accepted list and contradicts § 28.2, which grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County. Our redline conforms § 28.1 to New York law and New York County courts. **This finding did not pass verification and must be re-checked against the execution copy before it is raised.** The § 28.3 pre-suit executive escalation is acceptable process and is not flagged.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory on our playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than trading chips:

1. **No Vendor indemnity (no Section 20).** Absence of any IP indemnity is walk-away. Non-negotiable in substance, though we are flexible on drafting.
2. **§ 2.1 — three-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights.** Multi-year take-or-pay without an exit is walk-away; we require at minimum the 12-month reducible/true-up fallback.
3. **§ 7.2 — open-ended disclose-and-match.** Walk-away as both exclusive dealing and an open-ended MFN against us.
4. **§ 12.4 — 24-month, all-territory, undefined-scope non-compete.** Walk-away; deletion sought.
5. **§ 12.4 — no-hire covering all Vendor employees for term plus 24 months.** Walk-away; the 12-month mutual non-solicit fallback is the floor.
6. **§ 14.2 — revocable, non-transferable, term-limited Deliverable licence.** Walk-away; we need at minimum the perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free fallback.
7. **No termination for convenience against a three-year locked term.** Walk-away as combined with § 2.1.
8. **§ 28.1 — exclusive Singapore law and venue.** Walk-away as an exclusive foreign forum, subject to the verification point above.

We would highlight to Vendor that items 2, 3, 4 and 5 all contradict Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3. That inconsistency is our strongest lever and suggests these provisions may be template residue rather than a negotiated position.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Re-verify § 28.1** against the execution copy before circulating; the governing law finding failed verification and the apparent § 28.1 / § 28.2 conflict should be confirmed on the face of the document.
2. **Issue the redline** covering: new Section 20 (indemnity, remedies at 20.5); new § 9.4 (termination for convenience); new § 10.3 (transition and data return); revised § 2.1 (pay for what is ordered or used); deletion of the § 7.2 disclose-and-match; deletion of the § 12.4 non-compete; narrowing of the § 12.4 no-hire; and revision of § 14.2 (ownership and licence).
3. **Flag the duplicate numbering** to Vendor — there are two provisions numbered 7.2 and two numbered 12.4, and no Section 11 or Section 20 — and ask Vendor to confirm the intended structure so cross-references (§§ 9.3, 16.5, 19.4, 21.3, 30.5) resolve.
4. **Brief the business owner** on the § 2.1 commitment and the absence of any convenience exit, so we understand the commercial appetite before we concede on either.
5. **Confirm no further trading** on the compliant provisions (liability cap, assignment, audit, renewal, warranty, insurance) — these meet or exceed our positions and should not be reopened.

*Prepared on the basis of the verified findings supplied. No position is stated beyond those findings.*"}

It also conflicts with § 12.3 and with the Order Form fee structure in § 7.1. We have replaced it with pay-for-what-is-ordered-or-used, and offered the fallback in comment.

**§ 7.2 — Disclose-and-match (EXCLUSIVITY and MFN).** This single provision breaches two rules independently: as a sourcing restraint it is a de facto right of first refusal with no category limit, no 12-month sunset and no performance-failure exit; as an MFN it runs the wrong way, obliging us to extend Vendor any better third-party terms with no comparability carve-outs. Both fail the respective fallbacks and both contradict § 12.3. Our redline deletes the obligation and confirms Vendor's non-exclusive status.

**§ 12.4 — Non-compete (NONCOMPETE).** A 24-month post-term restraint on developing, marketing, selling or acquiring "any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory," with no internal-development or acquisition carve-out. Deletion is the minimal fix and restores consistency with § 12.3.

**§ 12.4 — No-hire (NOSOLICIT).** This is a no-hire rather than a non-solicit, covering all Vendor employees for the term plus 24 months "regardless of how the employee applies." We have narrowed it to our fallback — mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire. Outright deletion remains acceptable to us.

**No Section 20 — Indemnification (INDEMN).** No indemnity exists anywhere; the contiguous numbering confirms a drafting gap rather than an extraction error. We have inserted a Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorised access to Customer Data, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, extended to Customer Affiliates, with customary IP exclusions, a notice/control/cooperation procedure with a no-adverse-settlement carve-out, procure-modify-replace-refund remedies at § 20.5, and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and our breach of law. No super-cap was added because § 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims outside the cap — better than our fallback.

**§ 14.2 — Deliverable ownership and licence (IP and LICENSE).** Vendor owns every Deliverable created specifically for us, and our licence is revocable, non-transferable and limited to the Order Form term. This fails both the preferred position (Customer ownership with assignment) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense). The § 13.2 perpetual licence does not cure it — that covers Vendor Technology and embedded paid-up software, not the Deliverable. Our redline flips assignment to us while preserving Vendor Technology under § 14.3, and conforms the licence terms to §§ 13.1–13.3 (Affiliates and contractors, revocation only for uncured material breach).

**New § 9.4 — Termination for convenience (T4C).** Section 9 offers cause-based exits only, against a three-year term and a take-or-pay commitment with no termination right. We have added a Customer-only right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, expressly overriding the § 2.1 no-termination language for the terminated Services. Vendor has no convenience right, which is acceptable to us.

**New § 10.3 — Transition and data return (TRANSITION).** Section 10 covers only loss of access, Deliverable delivery and refunds; § 16.5 defers Customer Data to Sections 11 and 15, but Section 11 does not exist and Section 15 covers only processing purpose and privacy compliance. We have inserted up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable data return within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter, with backup and legal-retention carve-outs mirroring § 16.5.

**§ 28.1 — Governing law (GOVLAW).** Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction is outside our accepted list and contradicts § 28.2, which grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County. Our redline conforms § 28.1 to New York law and New York County courts. **This finding did not pass verification and must be re-checked against the execution copy before it is raised.** The § 28.3 pre-suit executive escalation is acceptable process and is not flagged.

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory on our playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than trading chips:

1. **No Vendor indemnity (no Section 20).** Absence of any IP indemnity is walk-away. Non-negotiable in substance, though we are flexible on drafting.
2. **§ 2.1 — three-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights.** Multi-year take-or-pay without an exit is walk-away; we require at minimum the 12-month reducible/true-up fallback.
3. **§ 7.2 — open-ended disclose-and-match.** Walk-away as both exclusive dealing and an open-ended MFN against us.
4. **§ 12.4 — 24-month, all-territory, undefined-scope non-compete.** Walk-away; deletion sought.
5. **§ 12.4 — no-hire covering all Vendor employees for term plus 24 months.** Walk-away; the 12-month mutual non-solicit fallback is the floor.
6. **§ 14.2 — revocable, non-transferable, term-limited Deliverable licence.** Walk-away; we need at minimum the perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free fallback.
7. **No termination for convenience against a three-year locked term.** Walk-away as combined with § 2.1.
8. **§ 28.1 — exclusive Singapore law and venue.** Walk-away as an exclusive foreign forum, subject to the verification point above.

We would highlight to Vendor that items 2, 3, 4 and 5 all contradict Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3. That inconsistency is our strongest lever and suggests these provisions may be template residue rather than a negotiated position.
